items.title: Will renewed conflict derail Ethiopia's economic growth?
items.summary: Ethiopia's economy is growing strongly. But renewed fighting in the north of the BRICS member state could deter investment, strain public finances and push up the cost of living Ethiopia 's economy is growing strongly. The International Monetary Fund (IMF) forecasts real growth of 9.2% for the 2025–26 fiscal year. But renewed fighting in the north , high reconstruction costs and climate-related crop problems are threatening the country's economic recovery London-based financial analyst Abdulmenan Mohammed warns of the consequences of further escalation . "If there is a major conflict [...] the current economic growth will not be sustainable," he told DW The war that raged in Tigray and other parts of Ethiopia between 2020 and 2022 inflicted extensive damage. Infrastructure was destroyed, businesses lost production capacity and agricultural land could no longer be cultivated in some areas A World Bank-backed damage and needs assessment puts the damage caused by several conflicts in Ethiopia between November 2020 and December 2021 at more than $22.6 billion (€20.2 billion).

items.title: Mozambique: 25 technicians trained in digital tools and rural business planning to improve access to finance
items.summary: The training took place from 19 to 29 October at the Macaneta Administrative Post, Marracuene district, and involved central-level technicians, Producer Organisation, Markets and Agribusiness Officers from the 11 Provincial Directorates of Agriculture and Fisheries (DPAP), as well as representatives of GAPI and Zambeze University (UniZambeze) The initiative aimed to strengthen participants’ capacities in using the RuralInvest (RIV20) platform, a digital tool designed for the preparation and analysis of business plans for investment in rural areas Photo: Ministério da Agricultura, Ambiente e Pescas The training forms part of the partnership between MAAP and the United Nations Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO), through its Investment Centre, under the PROMOVE Agribiz Project, funded by the European Union.

items.title: Government approves 20-year extension for Kenmare’s mining operations
items.summary: Maputo, 02 Nov (AIM) – The Irish company Kenmare Resources, which has been mining the heavy mineral sands in Moma and Larde districts, in the northern Mozambican province of Nampula, has announced that the Council of Ministers (cabinet) has approved a 20-year extension for its operations in the country. According to Miningmx, citing Kenmare’s statement addressed Mozambique’ stock exchange, agreement for the processing and export of heavy sands by Kenmare will run in until 2044. Royalties based on gross revenue will increase from one to three percent between 2025 and 2029, to four percent between 2030 and 2034, and to five percent between 2035 and 2044. Certain services contracted abroad are subject to a 20 percent withholding tax. “The company commits to investing at least 200 million dollars in equipment and infrastructure, plus an additional 50 million dollars in social projects, during the extension period”, said Kenmare Managing Director Tom Hickey, cieted in the document. He also downplayed the additional burden of the 200 million dollar commitment.

items.title: Mozambique: The marks of time on Avenida das Indústrias
items.summary: Companhia Vidreira de Moçambique, Caju de Moçambique, Zuid, Fibriclass [Fibreglass], Pintex, Mobilarte, Embalagens de Moçambique (Metal Box), FACOL – Fábrica de Colas e Adesivos de Moçambique, Metal África, Comec and Pro-Caju are just some of the names that left their mark on the industrial sector along that corridor. Decades later, many of these names survive only in collective memory and as geographical landmarks, associated, for example, with passenger transport stops Indeed, the current scene contrasts sharply with the dynamism of bygone years. Where industrial activity once thrived, all that remains are dilapidated buildings, ruins and premises left abandoned, while other facilities have been repurposed for new activities, particularly commerce, whose capacity to absorb labour is nowhere near that once provided by the former factories Companhia Vidreira de Moçambique, or simply Vidreira, founded in 1958 and described as the only facility of its kind in the country, is one of the industrial enterprises that still retains architectural features from the colonial period.

items.title: Fake nuclear warning from hacked app sparks unease but not panic in Ukraine
items.summary: Watch: Ukraine and Russia say emergency apps hit by cyber-attack Ukrainians have grown weary of the relentless alerts blaring from their phones and echoing through their streets, day and night, warning of Russian drones and missiles On Sunday night, the system delivered something to make them sit up and take note – a succession of more extreme threats that quickly escalated to impending nuclear strikes, chemical attacks and combat on the streets But many in the country did not take them seriously and doubted the veracity of the messages Sofia Kochmar, 34, a mother-of-one living in the western city of Lviv, said she was initially concerned but quickly questioned the authenticity of the alerts "The first thing I saw was the word 'nuclear' and that made me pretty nervous and scared.

items.title: If hackers can take control of a supermarket freezer, how vulnerable is other tech?
items.summary: Supermarkets across Europe have been hit by a suspected cyber-attack affecting their fridges and freezers, and raising concern about the vulnerabilities of internet-connected hardware from industrial machinery to humble domestic appliances Smart devices which are connected to the internet can include fridges, central heating, and even washing machines And while that makes them easier to control remotely, in theory, any device which goes online can potentially be exploited by malicious actors However, that doesn't mean hackers can easily take control of it, and big brands generally go to great lengths to make sure their tech is secure Exploits have been found before in some devices.
